groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

parts.context: A woman phones to volunteer for a river clean-up and asks about the arrangements.

transcript.text: Hello, River Friends, Paul speaking.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Hi Paul. My name's Anna Lopez, and I saw your poster at the library. I'd like to join the clean-up day.
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: Welcome aboard! We've had a lot of interest this year, which is great for the river.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: That's great news. We always need more people. Could you spell your surname for me?
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Yes, it's L-O-P-E-Z.
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: Thanks, Anna. Have you done anything like this before?
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: No, but I love being outside, and the river is very dirty at the moment, especially near my house.
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: That's fine. Last year, half of our volunteers had never done it before, and they all said they loved it.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: That's encouraging. I was a little worried I might not be useful.
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: It is. This year we're working on the stretch between the old bridge and the mill. We meet at the old bridge at nine o'clock.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Where exactly is that? Is it the stone bridge in the town centre?
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: No, that's the new bridge. The old bridge is the wooden one, about two kilometres upstream, next to the football field.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Okay, I think I know it. What date is the clean-up?
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: It's the first Sunday of next month, which is the sixth. If it rains, we'll move it to the following Sunday.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: What should I wear?
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: Old clothes and waterproof boots. It can get very muddy near the water. We provide gloves, rubbish bags and litter pickers.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: I have a good pair of boots in the cupboard, though I haven't worn them for ages.
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: They'll be perfect. The ground is wet whatever the weather, so it's best to be prepared.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: That's good. Do I need to bring any food?
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: We usually stop at twelve for lunch. The local bakery gives us sandwiches for free, but you should bring a bottle of water.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: I will. How long does the whole event last?
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: About five hours, though you can leave earlier if you need to. Some people only come for the morning.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Five hours is long, but I'm sure the time will pass quickly if the group is friendly.
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: It always does. We play music from a speaker, and there's usually plenty of laughter.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: And is there parking at the old bridge?
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: Only a few spaces. If possible, take the number twelve bus, which stops outside the football field. Or you could cycle.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: I'll take the bus. Is there anything else I should know?
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: One thing: please tell us if you have any allergies, because of the sandwiches. We can usually prepare something different.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: That's very kind. Thank you, Paul. See you there.
transcript.speaker: ANNA

transcript.text: See you there. Bring a smile!
transcript.speaker: PAUL
